players.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
players.verdict: High volume + elite efficiency and extreme solo-back splits make him the overall 1.01 target

players.name: Bijan Robinson
players.verdict: Paid, holdout resolved, every-down bell cow with strong receiving efficiency—cleanest RB1 profile

players.name: Ja'Marr Chase
players.verdict: 32% target share and 94% snaps keep him elite; 2025 dip was Burrow health, not talent decline.

players.name: Christian McCaffrey
players.verdict: Historic 2025 with elite receiving volume, but age-30 mileage and 2024 injury keep the floor honest

videoNotes.note: Far and away the leader in RB red-zone targets — the single biggest edge in the metric.

news.note: The 15-day absence was planned load management, not a setback: back in team drills Aug 23 with carries, 'I feel great, I feel fresh.' Shanahan said he'd have played in a normal game week.

players.name: Puka Nacua
players.verdict: League-best per-route WR with 30% target share and elite efficiency — a true 1.1-caliber WR anchor.

players.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
players.verdict: 36.8% target share and 0.90 WOPR — elite volume with a near-perfect 2025; only OC change tempers it.

players.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
players.verdict: Three straight top-5 finishes and 31.7% target share make him the safest WR outside the top four.

players.name: Jonathan Taylor
players.verdict: Bell-cow rusher with rare positive rush EPA, but thin passing role and 320+ touch mileage cap him

players.name: CeeDee Lamb
players.verdict: 2025 was TD-regression bad luck on missed games; volume and QB argue a rebound to WR1 range.

players.name: Justin Jefferson
players.verdict: Elite target share but a -0.81 rec EPA/g and unsettled QB room make this a rare risk at his price.

players.name: James Cook III
players.verdict: Locked-in rushing volume but heavily TD-fueled scoring and a thin 40-target receiving role

players.name: De'Von Achane
players.verdict: High volume plus explosive efficiency and heavy receiving role give a PPR-proof floor and top-5 ceiling

players.name: Chase Brown
players.verdict: Steady three-down back with a strong receiving floor—ceiling and floor both hinge on Burrow's health

videoNotes.note: 8 red-zone targets in 8 games with Burrow, and similar in 2024 — a real, repeated receiving role in the red zone, not a one-year blip. Smyth prices an RB red-zone target at 4.4x a normal carry, same as a goal-line carry.

players.name: Ashton Jeanty
players.verdict: Heavy volume but the warning quadrant—dreadful rush efficiency needs Kubiak's scheme to unlock it

players.name: Drake London
players.verdict: 33% target share with Penix healthy is WR1 volume; the whole case rides on the QB staying upright.

players.name: Omarion Hampton
players.verdict: Three-down breakout profile if healthy, but 2025 injury and Keaton Mitchell cap the confidence

players.name: Derrick Henry
players.verdict: Age-32 anomaly still rushing well, but pure-TD profile and the ever-present clock cap the case

players.name: Kenneth Walker III
players.verdict: Team change to KC is the upgrade—TD environment jumps, but efficiency and pass-down role are open

players.name: Saquon Barkley
players.verdict: 2024 spike regressed hard in 2025; big volume holds the floor but the ceiling needs efficiency back

players.name: Jeremiyah Love
players.verdict: Talented rookie but an unsettled three-way Arizona muddle makes the RB13 price too rich

videoNotes.note: Rostered by team 9, not a waiver target. Opens the season in a muddled committee (Braswell/Beck) so casual managers will undervalue him, but FSC expects his workload to ramp toward 17-18 PPG by the back half. Their call: buy-low trade around week 5 for roughly 4th-round redraft value.

news.note: High ankle sprain since Aug 13 preseason debut. Has not practiced or been on the field since; will not practice this week or play the preseason finale. Cardinals 'hopeful' for the Sept 13 opener; HC Mike LaFleur has not committed to Week 1.

players.name: Josh Jacobs
players.verdict: Fading trusty vet propped up by goal-line TDs in a committee-leaning Green Bay backfield

players.name: Josh Allen
players.verdict: Elite dual-threat workhorse with unmatched floor; 112 carries and QB1-caliber passing make him the safe QB1.

players.name: Breece Hall
players.verdict: Committee erosion cut his 2025, but receiving chops and an improved Jets offense keep bounce-back live

news.note: Groin strain, HC Aaron Glenn says 2-3 weeks, expected back for the opener. Board has him 13 slots ahead of market, so the miss matters more here than it does at ADP.

players.name: Brock Bowers
players.verdict: Elite bounce-back — 2024's 263-pt line and top red-zone share say the down 2025 was injury, not decline

players.name: Trey McBride
players.verdict: Elite volume TE1 — 27.9% target share and 169 looks are real, but a TD spike and QB downgrade cap the ceiling

players.name: Javonte Williams
players.verdict: Dallas rebound looked good, but low yds/tgt screams TD reliance and rookie Blue threatens the role

videoNotes.note: Red-zone-target leader but Smyth expects some decline from that rate; still projects a good share. Buy the role, not last year's exact number.

players.name: A.J. Brown
players.verdict: Clear-cut No. 1 in New England with a deep-ball QB fit; big ceiling, low floor on knee/hamstring risk.

players.name: Kyren Williams
players.verdict: Efficient and safe, but shrinking touch and goal-line share to Corum threatens the TD-based value

videoNotes.note: 3rd among RBs in red-zone routes — the passing-game red-zone role is priced into his floor, so a bad rushing TD split hurts him less than it looks.

players.name: Rashee Rice
players.verdict: 29% target share and elite red-zone role in KC, but knee ramp and Nagy's exit cloud the volume.

news.note: Post-May knee cleanup. Has not appeared in either preseason game. Chiefs beat reporter Nate Taylor: still 'laboring at times... in and out of breaks'. Rapoport reports no further NFL discipline expected for the probation violation.

players.name: George Pickens
players.verdict: 17.2 PPG and 2.13 pts/tgt even as Dallas's WR2 — a WR1-upside profile priced as a WR3.

players.name: Nico Collins
players.verdict: Clear alpha with 12.7 aDOT and strong per-target efficiency — a high floor if the health and O-line hold.

news.note: Jayden Higgins (projected starting X opposite him) tore his ACL and is out for the season. Collins is the unambiguous alpha in Houston.

players.name: Travis Etienne Jr.
players.verdict: Pass-catching rebound, but TD-fueled value plus a downgraded offense make me pass on the sleeper tag

players.name: Chris Olave
players.verdict: 29% target share and a WR7 finish when healthy; extension signed, clot cleared — buy the volume, fear the head.

news.note: Saints rookie WR2 Jordyn Tyson's hamstring has his regular season in serious doubt. ESPN moved Olave up to a lower-tier WR1; he ran a 30.3% target share over Weeks 10-18 last year after the Shaheed trade.

players.name: Malik Nabers
players.verdict: Rookie WR6 on top-of-NFL target volume, but knee recovery and a run-leaning Harbaugh offense cap it.

videoNotes.note: ACL recovery — avoided the PUP list (better than the 70-80% chance they gave it a month ago) but could still miss 1-3 games to start. ~80-90% odds of returning to pre-injury level, 20-25% reinjury risk over 2 years. Fine as a 3rd-round pick, too risky as a 2nd.

news.note: Shed the red no-contact jersey Aug 24, took 11-on-11 and 7-on-7 reps. Harbaugh: won't guarantee Week 1 but it's 'reasonable to assume that', and he 'moved the best we've seen this summer.'

players.name: Zay Flowers
players.verdict: WR12 in Lamar's 13 games with 30% target share; new pass-friendly OC could unlock a career year.

videoNotes.note: Quad contusion — minor, expected to miss only a few days of practice. Not a concern.

players.name: Garrett Wilson
players.verdict: 0.92 WOPR and 35% target share when healthy; talent is WR1-caliber, the offense and QB are not.

players.name: DeVonta Smith
players.verdict: Now Philly's undisputed No. 1 post-Brown trade; target share should jump toward 30% in a better scheme fit.

videoNotes.note: Hamstring injury, low concern — further along in recovery than the Eagles' rookie WR dealing with the same issue, and has existing chemistry with the QB. FSC expects him healthy for week 1 and is still drafting him at current price.

players.name: Cam Skattebo
players.verdict: Year-2 breakout bet with a three-down role, but weak efficiency and a crowded backfield temper it

videoNotes.note: Riser: 4 red-zone targets in only 6 games as a rookie — the ability showed up in a small sample.

expertSleeper.why: Emerging talent with a real jump in opportunity.

players.name: Tetairoa McMillan
players.verdict: 87% snaps and 45.9% air-yards share as a rookie; a clean Year-2 breakout if Bryce Young keeps climbing.

players.name: Colston Loveland
players.verdict: Late-rookie surge is the whole thesis — 20 PPG and 80% route share down the stretch point to a real leap

players.name: Emeka Egbuka
players.verdict: 20.5 PPG through five weeks as a rookie; now the clear No. 1 with Evans gone — big Year-2 upside.

players.name: Tyler Warren
players.verdict: Rock-steady sophomore — 21.5% target share and a 4.7 weekly stdev give the safest floor outside the top tier

players.name: Tee Higgins
players.verdict: Efficient, high-floor WR2 with WR1 upside whenever Burrow's healthy — injury risk is the only real knock.

players.name: Lamar Jackson
players.verdict: 2024 was a historic 430-point ceiling; rushing-TD decline and 2025 injury pull the range wide.

players.name: Drake Maye
players.verdict: League-best efficiency (CPOE 12.2, EPA 9.72) and rising volume; lowest-variance breakout at QB.

players.name: Jayden Daniels
players.verdict: Elite rushing volume and a 20.9 PPG rookie year; the 2025 injury, not talent, is the only knock.

players.name: Joe Burrow
players.verdict: Elite pocket passer with a passing-only QB1 ceiling; 2025 was injury, not decline — health is the bet.

players.name: Ladd McConkey
players.verdict: Year-3 breakout hopes hinge on a target share he doesn't yet own; 21% share and 0.50 WOPR are modest.

players.name: Bucky Irving
players.verdict: 2024 RB1 line proves the ceiling; 2025 was injury-wrecked, and healthy he's a high-volume, high-efficiency back

videoNotes.note: Shoulder dislocation/surgery, full camp participant and appears fully recovered; 10-20% instability/reinjury risk remains. FSC thinks the market hasn't repriced him despite the good news — backup Kenneth Gainwell profiles as a passing-down/2-minute back, not a real threat to his 65-70% share of TB touches.

Buy-low on volume: Tampa Bay was a top-10 red-zone-volume offense for RBs in 2024 (Irving over 2 combined RZ touches/game before injury cut his 2025 short). New OC should restore that passing-game RZ role; Gainwell/Sean Tucker will chip in but Smyth doesn't expect a repeat of last year's near-zero goal-line share.

players.name: Jaylen Waddle
players.verdict: New Denver WR1 role plus league-leading pass volume make this a strong ascending bet at a WR20s price.

players.name: Davante Adams
players.verdict: WR9 on TD volume, not efficiency (-106 yards-over-expected); regression looms behind Nacua.

players.name: Jalen Hurts
players.verdict: Tush-push rushing TDs anchor a solid floor, but the offense's 2025 slide and brutal playoff slate cap upside.

players.name: Quinshon Judkins
players.verdict: Poor per-touch data and a Sampson timeshare on a weak offense cap him at flex-plus

videoNotes.note: Negative: zero red-zone targets (as with Dobbins) — no pass-game red-zone role to fall back on.

players.name: Terry McLaurin
players.verdict: Elite in-game usage but 2025 efficiency crashed; Diggs caps ceiling — a volume bet on a Daniels rebound.

players.name: D'Andre Swift
players.verdict: Genuine three-down workhorse (223 car, 58% snaps) with rising rush EPA and a steady, low-variance floor

players.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
players.verdict: Elite per-route rookie on a bad offense — the one profile where a great TE still produces through the muck

players.name: David Montgomery
players.verdict: New team, 37% snaps and TD-reliant; the 2024 RB2 line masks shrinking usage behind Woody Marks

players.name: Sam LaPorta
players.verdict: Bounce-back bet — elite YAC and per-target efficiency on a great offense, if health and volume return

players.name: Bhayshul Tuten
players.verdict: Explosive talent but 2025 was a 21%-snap, 3.7-ypc committee sliver in a crowded JAX room

players.name: DJ Moore
players.verdict: Bounce-back bet on a Buffalo opening and Josh Allen after a dismal, low-efficiency 2025.
